review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it depends on: `lineRestriction`, `HasSecondOrderExpansionAt`, `HasSecondOrderExpansionAtCLM` and the existing `lineRestriction` simp lemmas in LineRestriction/Basic.lean. The only simp lemmas for `lineRestriction` are `lineRestriction_zero` and `lineRestriction_neg_direction`. There is no pointwise unfolding lemma, so every proof that needs one writes `simp [lineRestriction, ...]` (21 occurrences across 5 files, 6 in this file). I did not run Lean, so I claim no simp failure or loop. The suggested `@[simp] lineRestriction_apply` is a definitional rewrite whose right-hand side contains no `lineRestriction`, so it cannot loop. Whether it would conflict with the existing `lineRestriction_zero` is untested. Beyond that single interface issue I found nothing else, and the theorems themselves are plain implications, not simp candidates.

findings.declaration: HasSecondOrderExpansionAt.lineRestriction_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt (pattern also in lineRestriction_isLittleO, lineRestriction_at_hasSecondOrderExpansionAt and the CLM variants)
findings.problem: `lineRestriction` is a plain `def` with no pointwise unfolding lemma such as `lineRestriction u x v t = u (x + t • v)`. Only `lineRestriction_zero` and `lineRestriction_neg_direction` are tagged `@[simp]`. Every proof therefore adds the whole definition to the simp set, as in `simp [lineRestriction, ...]` at lines 41, 86, 106, 123, 168 and 189. Unfolding the constant is also less targeted than a lemma stated at an applied point. Several of these calls also pass the AC lemmas `mul_assoc`, `mul_left_comm` and `mul_comm` to close the arithmetic. These are heavy, order-sensitive simp sets, and nothing in the file shows why they are needed.
findings.proposed_change: In LineRestriction/Basic.lean, next to the definition, add `@[simp] theorem lineRestriction_apply (u : E → ℝ) (x v : E) (t : ℝ) : lineRestriction u x v t = u (x + t • v) := rfl`. The right-hand side contains no `lineRestriction`, so it cannot loop. Then replace `simp [lineRestriction, ...]` in this file with plain `simp` or `simp [lineRestriction_apply]`. Reduce the remaining arithmetic to a single `ring` step, or keep a minimal simp set after `simp only [lineRestriction_apply, ...]`.
findings.benefit: The unfolding of the definition becomes a named, reusable simp rule that `simp` applies at applied terms without a `simp [lineRestriction]` flag. The other users of `lineRestriction` get it too, including the 21 `simp [lineRestriction ...]` sites. The proofs here also become less sensitive to AC-rewrite order.

evidence.excerpt:
def lineRestriction (u : E → ℝ) (x v : E) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun t ↦ u (x + t • v)

lineRestriction u x v 0 = u x := by
  simp [lineRestriction]
